case.title: Science fair venue, budget and volunteers

canvasName: R2-C06 Science fair venue, budget and volunteers

segments.text: Thank you for coming to the science fair planning meeting. We have about forty minutes and we need to leave with a budget, a schedule, a venue plan, and named owners. The fair is for grades six through eight, it will run on a Saturday in October, and we expect one hundred and twenty student projects. Last year we had eighty projects and it was already crowded, so this year we need a different layout.
segments.textReply: I’m capturing the meeting scope and the key constraint: project count rises from 80 to 120 after last year’s crowding.

segments.text: Let's start with the goal. The fair should be a low pressure opportunity for students to explain their work, not a pure competition. Every student gets a table and a short presentation slot. We will have three judged categories: scientific method, engineering design, and communication. We also want a family open house in the afternoon so parents and younger students can visit.
segments.textReply: I’m adding the event goals as a new panel: student-centered presentations, three judged categories, and an afternoon family visit.

segments.text: The venue options are the school gym, the cafeteria plus hallway, and the community college atrium. The gym is free and can hold one hundred and twenty tables, but the acoustics are terrible and the floor is needed for basketball on Friday night, so setup cannot start until seven in the morning.

segments.text: The cafeteria and hallway can hold ninety tables and setup can start Friday afternoon, but the hallway is a fire lane and we cannot block it. The college atrium is beautiful and has parking, but it costs eight hundred dollars and requires a certificate of insurance. The safety requirements are not optional. Every project using heat, chemicals, or live animals needs a pre approval form signed by a teacher.

segments.text: No open flames. Electrical projects must use grounded outlets and cannot daisy chain power strips. We need two first aid stations and a clear path for emergency vehicles. The district safety officer has to review the floor plan two weeks before the event. The budget we have is four thousand dollars from the PTA, plus whatever we raise.

This year we want to add a keynote speaker and a livestream for families who cannot attend. The speaker honorarium is five hundred, the AV rental is seven hundred, and the livestream requires a volunteer and a dedicated laptop. Let's compare the two realistic venue plans.

segments.text: Plan A is the gym plus the outdoor courtyard for food trucks. Capacity is good, setup is painful, and the acoustics are poor. Plan B is the cafeteria, the hallway, and four classrooms for quiet presentations. Capacity is ninety projects, so we would need to limit entries or run two sessions. The college atrium is a third option but the insurance and cost make it a stretch.

The atrium remains a costly, insurance-dependent stretch option.

segments.text: The committee's preference is Plan A if we can solve three problems: setup time, noise, and power. The custodial team says they can open the gym at six, not seven, if we submit a request two weeks ahead. The AV club can lend us two portable speakers and six microphones. The facilities team can bring in two quiet generators for the courtyard, but we need to keep them away from the presentation tables.

shapes.html:
Science Fair · Grades 6–8
Purpose: a low-pressure Saturday fair in October for up to 120 student projects, where students explain their work and families can visit.
Consensus decisions
  • Venue: Plan A — school gym + courtyard; quiet corner and small entrance PA. Atrium is backup only if gym is unavailable.
  • Capacity: registration capped at 120; form opens next Monday and closes three weeks before the fair.
  • Budget: approve $3,100; hold $900 contingency from $4,000 PTA funds. Receipts due within two weeks.
  • Access: temporary ramp at courtyard door; reserve front row for wheelchairs and strollers. Registration asks about accessibility needs.
Plan & safety essentials
  • Request 6:00 a.m. gym access from custodians two weeks ahead; AV club lends 2 speakers + 6 microphones; facilities supplies 2 quiet generators away from tables.
  • Engineering projects near courtyard; reading/communication in quiet corner; use entrance PA, not gym sound system.
  • Teacher sponsor and signed safety form required at registration; special approval for heat, chemicals, or live animals. No flames; grounded outlets only; no daisy-chained strips.
  • Keep fire lane and emergency vehicle access clear; provide two first-aid stations. District safety officer reviews floor plan two weeks before event.
Owners & deadlines
OwnerActionDue
Ms. ChenVenue request + safety floor plan4 weeks before
Mr. PatelBudget + receipts3 weeks before; receipts within 2 weeks
PTA liaisonSnack order + volunteer signup2 weeks before
AV clubPA + livestream test1 week before
Meeting lead (name not captured)Registration form + judge assignment; send minutes + create shared checklistForm opens next Monday; minutes/checklist tonight
Event-day timeline
8:00 setup · 9:00 welcome/safety · 9:30–11:30 judging · 11:30–12:30 lunch/family open house · 12:30–2:00 public viewing/demos · 2:00–2:30 keynote · 2:30–3:00 awards/cleanup · clear gym by 4:00.
Judges rotate in pairs (≤12 projects/pair); presentations use 15-minute blocks + 5-minute transitions.
Open risks & communication
Volunteer gap: need 12 judges, 4 check-in, 2 first aid, 2 floaters, 1 AV lead; confirmed 6 judges + 2 check-in. Outreach may send 5 students (service-hours forms); recruit remaining help via high-school science club. If fewer than 10 judges at T−2 weeks: switch to poster walk and shorten judging by 30 minutes.
Emails: families this week (date/link); teachers next week (safety); T−2 weeks (drop-off map); day before (parking/lunch). Newsletter: short paragraph + last-year photo.
